deep.reconstruction:
Overview. The page holds combinatorial bookkeeping in a private symbolic notation and has no running text. The verso it sits behind is a personal letter from Riemann's brother Wilhelm, so this is scrap paper. The next folio continues the same notation with genus-dependent exponents (b'^5 a'^1 b^{p-3} a^{p-1}, ...) and with sums such as a+a'+Σb or Σa·0. That points to point-groups or divisors on a genus-p surface, or to classes of theta characteristics, sorted by how many points of each of four kinds (a, a', b, b') they contain. Nothing on the page is a finished derivation, and every interpretation below is my hypothesis.

(A) Top left block. The headings are a'+b+c+Σ∂, c'+a+b+Σa', and b'acΣ∂. Below them is a column of 'words' such as abcΣ∂'Σ∂, ∂_1Σa'bcΣ∂, ac∂'_1Σc'Σ∂, abc∂'_1Σc'Σa', ∂_1abcΣa'∂'_2 and ∂_2abcΣa'∂'_2. Each word reads as a sum of points: single named points plus Σ of a whole class, with primes marking a second class. Riemann appears to list all the ways a group of fixed type can be completed from a pool of points of types a, b, c, ∂ and their primed partners.
- A middle column (a'_1bc∂_1∂'_2, a'_2a'_1∂'_1∂_1∂_2, ...) is followed by a numbered list: 4) a a'_1; 3) a'_2 b c ∂'_1; 2) ∂_1∂_2∂'_2; 1) b'_1b'_2c'_1c'_2.
- This list looks like a partition of the points into four groups.
- The right-hand tableau has rows labelled ab, a, b and pairs entries like c'_1c_1c_2a with ∂_1∂_2. It looks like a table of compatible groups, i.e. which group can be paired with which.

(B) Top right block. It starts from b_1a_3a_4Σa and b_1b_5b_6Σa, then a_1a_2 b_3b_4 = a_1b_3 a_2b_4 and a_1b_4 a_2b_3. This regroups the two pairs {a_1,a_2},{b_3,b_4} into the two possible mixed pairings. The labels p_1,p_2 and q_1,q_2 attached to aΣc c'_1 and ab c'_2 c suggest naming the resulting groups.

(C) Middle block: products of 'brackets'. Riemann writes expressions such as a_1(a_2a_3δ_1 · a_2a_3δ_2 · a_2a_3a_4δ_3) and the analogues with a_2 and a_3 pulled out, then the same with a_4 in place of a_3.
- Each pulled-out a_i is followed by brackets in the remaining a's together with δ_1, δ_2 (three-letter brackets) and δ_3 (four-letter brackets).
- He then writes a quotient: [a_1a_3δ_1][a_1a_3δ_2][a_2a_4δ_1][a_2a_4δ_2] − [a_1a_4δ_1][a_1a_4δ_2][a_2a_3δ_1][a_2a_3δ_2] ..., all over [a_1a_2δ_1][a_1a_2δ_2]. A further product [a_3a_4δ_1][a_3a_4δ_2] is written below it.
- One reading of the three-letter brackets is 3×3 determinants of points in the plane. The Grassmann–Plücker relation then gives, for each fixed δ: [13δ][24δ] − [14δ][23δ] = [12δ][34δ].
- On that reading the numerator is x_1x_2 − y_1y_2, with x_k = [13δ_k][24δ_k], y_k = [14δ_k][23δ_k] and x_k − y_k = [12δ_k][34δ_k]. Division by [12δ_1][12δ_2] then simplifies part of it, which would explain why the product [34δ_1][34δ_2] appears beneath. The numerator is unfinished ('−...'), so the computation cannot be completed from the page.
- The four-letter brackets with δ_3 do not fit 3×3 determinants. Their meaning, whether theta-constants labelled by sets of branch points or something else, is undetermined.

(D) The displayed identity. It reads (a_3 a_4)·[a_1a_2δ_1][a_1a_2δ_2][a_1a_2a_4δ_3][a_1a_2a_3δ_3] = (a_1 a_2)·[a_2a_3a_4δ_3][a_1a_3a_4δ_3][a_3a_4δ_1][a_3a_4δ_2].
- The right side is exactly the image of the left side under the index swap 1↔3, 2↔4. Riemann is therefore asserting that this expression is invariant under the swap, which is what a symmetric normalisation requires.
- If (a_i a_j) means a difference a_i − a_j and the brackets are theta-constants labelled by subsets of branch points, this has the shape of a Thomae/Rosenhain-type relation between hyperelliptic theta-constant products and branch-point differences. That reading is a guess.

(E) Lower half: more partition bookkeeping. Riemann now uses indexed points a_1…a_6 and b_1…b_8 and splits them into blocks separated by commas and vertical bars.
- Examples: b_1 a_1a_2a_3a_4 , b_2b_3b_4b_5b_6 | b_1b_2b_3a_1a_2  b_4b_5b_6a_3a_4 | a_5 ... Σb.
- A small tableau a_5 | a_6 over b_8 is followed by a final array a_5a_6 | a_6  b_1a_1a_2  a_3a_4 over b_7b_8 | b_7b_8  b_4b_5b_6  b_2b_3 =, left unfinished.
- This continues the enumeration of ways to split the a- and b-points into groups of prescribed composition. It matches the systematic count with exponents in p on the next folio.
errors: Nothing on the page can be shown to be wrong, because the meaning of the symbols is not fixed by the page itself.
The quotient in the middle block is left incomplete: the numerator trails off with '−...'.
The final equation at the bottom of the page ends in '=' with no right-hand side.
Several entries are struck out (for example 'a_3' at the start of the third bracket line, 'b_1a_1 a_2a_3', and 'a_5a_6 + a_1a_2 a_3a_4'). These are false starts that Riemann himself abandoned.

results.what: Systematic enumeration of point-groups or partitions of special points (a, a', b, b', c, ∂ classes) on a genus-p surface, apparently for classifying divisors or characteristics.
results.modern_name: Combinatorics of theta characteristics or special divisors (partitions of branch or special points)

results.what: Invariance of the bracket product (a_3a_4)[12δ1][12δ2][124δ3][123δ3] under the index swap (1↔3, 2↔4).
results.modern_name: Possibly a Thomae/Rosenhain-type relation among theta-constant products, or a symmetric bracket identity
results.usually_credited_to: Rosenhain (1851), Thomae (1870) if the theta reading is correct

results.what: Quotient built from products of three-term brackets, consistent with the Plücker relation [13δ][24δ] − [14δ][23δ] = [12δ][34δ].

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary private combinatorial scratch notes of a kind Riemann is known to have made on theta functions and characteristics. No identifiable result goes beyond standard material; the possible Thomae-type relation is speculative and not explicit.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; P=[Matrix(symbols(f'x{i} y{i}'))for i in range(5)]; B=lambda i,j,k: Matrix([[P[i][0],P[i][1],1],[P[j][0],P[j][1],1],[P[k][0],P[k][1],1]]).det(); simplify(B(1,3,0)*B(2,4,0)-B(1,4,0)*B(2,3,0)-B(1,2,0)*B(3,4,0))==0
checkable.asserts: Plücker three-term relation [13δ][24δ] − [14δ][23δ] = [12δ][34δ] for points in the plane (δ = point 0). This is the identity that would make the middle-block quotient simplify.
The right-hand side of the displayed identity is the image of the left-hand side under the swap 1↔3, 2↔4 (the prefactor (a3 a4) correspondingly maps to (a1 a2)).

transcription_corrections: Top right line 1: 'b_1 a_3 a_4 Σa' is probably 'b_1 a'_3 a_4 Σa' or similar; the primes in this corner are uncertain.

In the second bracket line, 'a_2 a_1 a_4 δ_1 a_1 a_4 δ_2' carries superscript marks (prime or 7) over the δ's that the transcription omits; similar marks appear over δ in a_1(a_2a_4δ_1 a_2a_4δ_2 ...).
Left column, line 6: 'abc ∂'_1 Σc' Σa'' — the leading letters look like 'abc' with a correction mark; the transcription is plausible.
Bottom right 'ΣL' or 'Σb' near 'a_5 a_6' (struck) is written faintly; 'Σb' is plausible.
'Riemann 19' and '50' are archival labels and '76' at right margin is the folio number; none of them is mathematics.
